answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a slashable stake. To claim a seat on the ledge, each identity locks collateral, and any signed message that contradicts another key forfeits it. A falcon fleet of fakes therefore needs a separate bond per account, so growing the swarm grows the bill. When correlation checks link those keys at the wharf, the whole cluster is slashed at once. The attacker funds every false identity up front and loses the entire hoard on the first conflicting signature, making a mass army far costlier than one honest participant's single deposit.
